result.summary: Read lib/letflow/design/req156-lua-memory-limit-impl.md end to end (all 348 lines) and re-grepped the entire document for `fn `, `raise `, `case `, `cond `, `do:`, `->`. The §5 line-181 violation from the prior FAIL is confirmed fixed: the table cell now reads as prose ('submitted to Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor via async_nolink/2, with the supervisor as the first argument and a zero-argument closure over the script source and budget as the second, exactly as REQ-155 §4.1-§4.3 already specify, byte-for-byte') -- no fn/anonymous-function literal, no callable expression. The full-document re-grep found zero fn/raise/do:/-> hits anywhere, and every 'case'/'cond' hit is genuine English prose (lines 26, 113, 167, 181, 197, 203, 204, 214, 229, 333, 346 -- e.g. 'memory-kill case', 'REQ-155's case', 'unconditional', 'conditioned on', and one meta-reference '`case`/`cond` in a test' describing how a future test would pattern-match, not an actual code fragment). Design is exhaustively clean of literal implementation code. All 7 previously-passed checks spot-checked and still intact: AC mapping (§8, all 7 ACs mapped, unchanged), the source-verified async_nolink/Task.Supervisor limitation claim (§2, unchanged, cites task/supervisor.ex and task/supervised.ex), the alternative spawn_opt/monitor mechanism (§2 and §5, still coherent and complete), the :killed-reason race resolution (§5.3, still structural/ordering-based and sound), error-shape distinguishability (§4.1, three structurally distinct shapes unchanged), moduledoc content requirements (§7, all 5 items present and unchanged), open questions (§10, OQ-1..OQ-5 all present with blocking/non-blocking dispositions stated, none silently resolved). No regression from the rework edit.
